resources.string: How fibroblasts maintain the dermal matrix
A simplified view of normal human dermal matrix support and repair. The cue and fiber changes are schematic and not to scale.
Beneath the epidermis, fibroblasts sit among bundles of collagen. These bundles are part of the extracellular matrix, the supporting material around the cells.
Local signals during normal tissue repair can prompt nearby fibroblasts to make more matrix. The pulse represents a cue, not a visible wound.
Fibroblasts release collagen precursors and other matrix proteins. Outside the cells, collagen assembles into fibrils that add to the fiber network.
As the matrix remodels, fibers can shift and form bundles that run in different directions. The new fibers become part of the existing network.
Parts of the older matrix are broken down and replaced as new matrix is made. The collagen network helps the dermis resist stretching.
